title: Menu key press on a desktop applet opens context menu in the top left corner of the screen
line: Pressing the Menu key on the desktop or a desktop widget now opens the context menu centred on it instead of in the top left corner of the screen.
explanation: ContainmentItem::keyPressEvent turns the Menu key into a synthetic right-button mouse event, but passed an empty global position. The menu is popped at the event's global position, so it always appeared at (0,0); the local position also used the focused item's top-left corner, which for the desktop is (0,0) too. The change uses the centre of the focused item (or of the containment if nothing has focus) and maps it to global coordinates.

commits.message:
containmentitem: open the Menu key context menu near the focused item

Pressing the Menu key built a fake mouse event with no global position,
so the desktop or applet context menu always opened at the top left
corner of the screen. Use the centre of the focused item, mapped to it.

BUG: 477114

media.caption: Menu key on the empty desktop: menu at the top left corner
Menu key on the empty desktop: menu centred on the desktop
Menu key while typing in a Sticky Note: note's menu at the top left corner
Menu key while typing in a Sticky Note: note's menu opens at the note's centre

review.text: Accurate root-cause fix in libplasma's ContainmentItem::keyPressEvent: previously the synthetic right-button QMouseEvent for Qt::Key_Menu passed an empty global position QPointF(), causing QMenu::popup() to open at (0, 0). Computing localPos as the center of the focused item (falling back to the containment center) and passing mapToGlobal(localPos) properly positions both desktop and applet context menus and works cleanly with applet hit-testing and Wayland/multi-monitor coordinates. Before/after screenshots confirm both the empty desktop and Sticky Note applet cases.
